import FormalConjecturesUtil
/-!

# Erdős Problem 354
*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/354](https://www.erdosproblems.com/354)

-/
namespace Erdos354

/-- The sequence `⌊a⌋, ⌊γ * a⌋, ⌊γ ^ 2 * a⌋, ..., ⌊γ ^ i * a⌋, ...`. -/
noncomputable def FloorMultiples (a γ : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : ℤ := ⌊γ ^ n * a⌋

/-- The sequence `⌊a⌋, ⌊b⌋, ⌊γ * a⌋, ⌊γ * b⌋, ... ⌊γ ^ i * a⌋, ⌊γ ^ i * b⌋, ...` -/
noncomputable def FloorMultiples.interleave (a b γ : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : ℤ :=
  if n % 2 = 0 then
    FloorMultiples a γ (n / 2)
  else
    FloorMultiples b γ (n / 2)

/-- Let $\alpha,\beta\in \mathbb{R}_{>0}$ such that $\alpha/\beta$ is irrational. Is the multiset
$$\{ \lfloor \alpha\rfloor,\lfloor 2\alpha\rfloor,\lfloor 4\alpha\rfloor,\ldots\}\cup
\{ \lfloor \beta\rfloor,\lfloor 2\beta\rfloor,\lfloor 4\beta\rfloor,\ldots\}$$ complete? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_354.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (α > 0) (β > 0), Irrational (α / β) →
    IsAddCompleteNatSeq' (FloorMultiples.interleave α β 2) := by
  sorry

/-- Let $\alpha,\beta\in \mathbb{R}_{>0}$ such that $\alpha/\beta$ is irrational. Is
$$\{ \lfloor \alpha\rfloor,\lfloor \gamma\alpha\rfloor,\lfloor \gamma^2\alpha\rfloor,\ldots\}\cup
\{ \lfloor \beta\rfloor,\lfloor \gamma\beta\rfloor,\lfloor \gamma^2\beta\rfloor,\ldots\}$$ complete? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_354.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ γ ∈ Set.Ioo (1 : ℝ) 2, ∀ᵉ (α > 0) (β > 0), Irrational (α / β) →
    IsAddCompleteNatSeq' (FloorMultiples.interleave α β γ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos354

reformulations.difference: The source's two finite exponent sets and sufficiently large natural numbers are represented by one finite subset of an interleaved integer-valued sequence and eventuality at Filter.atTop on ℤ.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Positions 2s and 2t+1 supply the α and β terms respectively. Splitting any finite index set by parity gives exactly the source's finite sets S,T; conversely, their even and odd images give the interleaved index set. Equal values at different positions remain independently usable. Eventuality on ℤ is equivalent to eventuality on natural-number casts, by replacing an integer cutoff N with N.toNat, and conversely casting a natural cutoff. The equivalence, including all quantifiers and an arbitrary propositional answer slot, was proved in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean.

reformulations.difference: The gamma variant uses the same interleaved integer-sequence encoding instead of the source's two finite sums of floored gamma powers.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The parity reindexing and integer/natural cutoff equivalence hold for every fixed α, β, γ. They therefore remain equivalent under the positivity and irrationality hypotheses, the universal α,β quantifiers, the existential γ ∈ (1,2), and the answer equivalence. This full equivalence was also proved in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean.

sources_consulted: https://www.erdosproblems.com/354 — statement, remarks, gamma variant, and current OPEN status; read through the rendered HTML at https://r.jina.ai/https://www.erdosproblems.com/354.

P. Erdős and R. L. Graham, Old and New Problems and Results in Combinatorial Number Theory (1980), pp. 56–58, especially the question on p. 58: https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~ronspubs/80_11_number_theory.pdf.
R. L. Graham, On Sums of Integers Taken from a Fixed Sequence (1971), definition of completeness on p. 24 and Open Questions, Problem 12: https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~ronspubs/71_08_integer_sums.pdf.
